recipes.name: Peg's Summer Squash Bake
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup butter, cut into small chunks

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Put squash slices in a single layer in the bottom of a 9x12-inch baking dish. Dot with butter; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until squash is tender, bubbling, and golden brown, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Peg's Summer Squash Bake
raw_recipe.description: Peg's summer squash bake recipe features oven-baked summer squash, butter, and Parmesan. Enhance it further by adding other vegetables and more cheese.

review.reviewBody: I could die and go to heaven right now, having succumbed to culinary bliss. I used 'space ship' squash (small, yellow summer squash) and followed the recipe, but I added a few things. Following the advice of previous raters, I cooked mine for about 40 minutes. I added a drizzle of olive oil, sliced red pepper, fresh garlic, and a sprinkle of basil. Additionally, I had some green chille pepper from my garden that I diced and through in. The result was beyond delicious and so easy!

Just exactly what I was looking for. Straight forward, no cream soups, fresh and delicious. I added seasonings of choice with some chopped green onion and baked in my counter top oven. Deleting all my other heavy squash recipes, this is so good. I even prepped it ahead of time and put back in the fridge until the rest of my meal was almost done. Thanks for sharing!
Very easy to make! I used both zucchini and summer squash. I melted the butter and brushed it on. Loved this!

Better than I expected! I tried this recipe because it was simple, but I didn't really think it'd be a hit. I have made it twice this week already. The second time, I simply melted maybe 1 T butter in my pan, laid in the squash, sprinkled with garlic salt, and then parm. Sharp cheddar is also good on this.

This was really good. I only made minor minor changes. I shredded the squash with a grater instead of slicing it. It cooked in about twenty minutes that way. I also turned the oven up to 425. Instead of only using Parmesan I used an Italian blend with parmesan alone, Romano, and Parmesan all mixed in together. About five minutes before I took it out I added some fresh basil to the pan and then browned the top. It was amazing. Will definitely make again.

I peeled the squash and zucchini (one small of each). My wife has stomach issues can’t digest. Sprayed 9x9 glass pan with Pam—a mistake. Plenty of grease with cheese and butter. I put drained diced tomatoes on one side to try, was wonderful. Didn’t have fancy Parmesan (only green can Kraft) I used 1/8 cup mixed with seasoned Panko along with 1/8 cup shredded mozzarella. It came out crispy on top but a bit greasy on bottom. I drained on paper towels a bit. Was great that way.

This was good. I added peppers and onions as suggested along with some rosemary, tossed the veggies in olive oil and omitted the butter. It took longer than the recommended time to cook, and I ended up raising the oven temperature to 450 to hurry it along, since the rest of my meal was ready and waiting.

Used sliced patty pan squash from my garden. Added
Some onion powder as well. Had to cook longer, about 35 minutes and turned on the broiler to crisp up the cheese for a few minutes at the end. Great recipe - thanks!

I used yellow squash, green pepper and an onion cut in rings. I chose to add some garlic powder and a pinch of pepper to the Parmesan cheese , melted the butter to drizzle it over the cheese mixture then sprinkled Italian seasoning over all before cooking it for 30 minutes. It was excellent!

This is simple but really good and it makes a pretty side dish. One yellow squash does not cut it for my family of 3 but then my husband has always said I was born to cook for a family of 6. I used 2 very large summer squashes with the same amount of butter. I thinly sliced some onion and threw that in the dish and seasoned with salt, garlic powder and italian seasoning. I didn't measure the parmesan just eyeballed it until it looked like it was enough for me. Everything couldn't lay in a single layer so I needed to bake it for about 30 minutes. What I like the most about the dish is it frees you up to cook other stuff. PS I think 1/4 cup of butter would be way too much for just one squash, so butter accordingly or you will be swimming in butter...not that that is always bad mind you.....

Yummy! I actually sauteed mine on the stove top with some olive oil. I added a bit of garlic and onion, also. I also tossed in some fresh basil because I got a LOT with my CSA this go-round (also the reason for needing a squash recipe!) The parmesan cheese in this is simply divine!! Can't wait for the leftovers today at lunch!

So simple with few ingredients, but SO very tasty. I took the recipe submitter’s suggestion and added some chopped red bell pepper for a pop of color. I gave it a good grind of both salt and pepper but no other additions. Took an extra 5 mins to reach that crisp-tender stage, but definitely not overcooked or mushy. I do think a sprinkle of crisp, crumbled bacon would be the perfect topper, but I’m not complaining without it. This one’s a keeper!
Yummy might have added slightly more butter and cheese, but they came out great
I was skeptical at first, but I used Italian seasoning and salt and pepper. I was pleasantly surprised that such a simple recipe could taste so good. Definitely a keeper.
Easy and tasty.
Instead of butter, we used olive oil spray. Additionally, we sliced zucchini with the squash and seasoned with Italian seasoning. It was quick and easy but a bit bland.

Aaaaamazing!! The only thing I changed was I used Roasted Garlic Cheese because I didn’t have any Parmesan on hand ??????

Super easy to make. Added a few seasonings but other than that, went by directions. I think I might add Italian bread crumbs on top next time. Will make again as it is a good easy basic recipe to go by..
It was excellent went well with my roasted chicken.
